{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.0) or shows early negative signals (e.g., -0.25), as market sentiment often underestimates downside risk.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >70% from prior peak) by applying a 10-15% dampening factor to prevent overcorrection.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% to align with historical volatility patterns.",
    "For long-term horizons (>15 days), reduce forecast volatility by 15-20% if sentiment is neutral or negative, to reflect reduced speculative momentum.",
    "When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.33), allow forecast to rise but cap growth at 5% above prior 7-day high to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days), apply a downward bias of 2-5% to correct for model overconfidence.",
    "For short-term (1-5 day) forecasts, prioritize alignment with recent 3-day moving average to reduce lag errors."
  ]
}
